description: Compilation of open-plus-controlled extraction forms for the accessible studies in this review, repaired for extraction_codebook.json v1.1 using per-paper siloed subagent reasoning passes. Controlled-code summaries are preserved per study; loose keyword categorization is not used.
method_notes: This index recompiles the existing accessible-corpus extractions after the protocol/codebook v1.1 migration; no search or retrieval was rerun.
Each paper received a siloed pi -p subagent reasoning pass focused only on v1.1 fields: generality/reuse mechanism, IVV integration level, and reliability subtype.

Subagents saw only protocol.md, extraction_codebook.json, the paper markdown, and that paper's existing extraction; they returned JSON patches with exact controlled labels, rationale, evidence, and confidence.

Claim-level reliability_subtype retains not applicable where appropriate; the structured summary lists substantive reliability/reliability-adjacent subtypes when present to keep aggregate synthesis interpretable.

validation_summary.notes: Automated validation confirmed all v1.1 controlled fields are present in every extraction, selected controlled values match extraction_codebook.json exactly, selected codes have rationale/evidence/confidence, and every selected limitation flag has an assessment.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Define CubeSat behaviors from mission requirements through functional architecture using MBSE/SysML, motivated by high university CubeSat failure rates and intuition-driven design.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Enterprise-level black-box use cases for 'CubeSat Enterprise' interacting with a Chief Scientist, then decomposition into Ground Segment and Space Segment activities and lower-level actions. minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Starts from a well-defined set of mission requirements; does not show elicitation/validation of a full mission requirements set.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_or_domain_know: Requires well-defined mission requirements and enough stakeholder/mission-tasking knowledge to identify actors, use cases, preconditions, triggers, postconditions, and scenarios. key_method_quotes: Abstract: 'This paper describes an eight-step approach for defining the behaviors of CubeSats that begins with mission requirements and ends with a functional architecture modeled as an activity hierarchy using... SysML.'

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper presents a repeatable eight-step method tied to the CubeSat Reference Model and uses generic CubeSat mission-data requirements/use cases that teams can tailor to unique missions. High-level abstraction and mission-agnostic architecture are supported only at the generic CubeSat enterprise / mission-data functional-architecture level. Do not code interface-focused model because interfaces are future work; do not code low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model because limited behavior detail is a scope limitation, not a claimed reuse mechanism; do not code specific-mission model with reusable method only because the examples are generic/reference-model examples, not a named specific mission.

evidence.quote: This approach provides a repeatable, generalized method for CubeSat development teams to follow
the SSWG's recent effort has been focused on the development of a CubeSat Reference Model to be used by university CubeSat teams, though it could be used by any CubeSat development team

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Small satellites are constrained by mass, power, volume, schedule, and cost; subsystem functions are coupled by data, energy, and access times; conventional CubeSat design/operations rely on intuition, simplified trades, and ad hoc/unverified simulator coupling. The paper extends an MBSE framework by modeling RAX operational behaviors/scenarios and integrating simulation tools to drive analysis/design.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: RAX mission model with launch, environment, mission, operations, flight, and ground systems; focus is the RAX Mission and primarily logical subsystem models, with selected physical components referenced as realizations (e.g., battery hardware implements store-energy function).
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Launch and environment are recognized but not the paper focus; physical subsystem detail is secondary to logical operations; ADCS, thermal, structures, and mechanisms are passive/self-explanatory for RAX; SNR assumes one ground station; simulations are not yet unified; real-data validation is future work.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Requires CubeSat mission/subsystem knowledge, operations scheduling concepts, orbital/access/solar context, link-budget and power/energy equations, and tool skills in SysML/MagicDraw, STK, MATLAB, PHX ModelCenter, ParaMagic, and CST. Beginners found SysML easier with prior CubeSat mission or tool experience.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: Uses a CubeSat-specific SysML framework/meta-model, logical/physical separation, modular subsystem/state/interaction decomposition, acausal parametric constraints, and an analysis-driven rule that model elements are introduced only when needed for an executable analysis/simulation.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper is RAX-applied, but it explicitly frames the work as a CubeSat community framework/model-development-kit and template, not merely a one-off RAX model. Do not add low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model because executable dynamics, power scenarios, and state/activity behavior are central. Do not add specific-mission model with reusable method only because the paper claims a reusable CubeSat framework/template beyond RAX.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_data_flow: MagicDraw/SysML stores structural, behavioral, parametric, and requirement-related model artifacts. ParaMagic executes SysML parametrics and can update solved values back into SysML. PHX ModelCenter orchestrates STK scenarios and MATLAB scripts using wrappers and graphical data links, automatically transferring data between simulators. CST executes/animates state-machine and activity models. STK provides orbit/access/solar visualization and analysis; MATLAB provides custom computations.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity_evidence: The paper argues that SysML is formal, human-readable, and machine-interpretable; continuity is illustrated by SysML parametric models executed in ParaMagic and SysML diagrams projected to PHX ModelCenter workflows, but formal semantic consistency checks are not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Behavior models include ground/flight interface, OBC command dispatch, and communications states, supporting mission software/interface V&V in principle. EPS hardware integration, flat-sat/HIL, and environmental tests are not reported.
toolchain_limitations: wrapper setup and save/reopen cycles are time-consuming
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: No public SysML model, scripts, wrapper files, scenarios, or data are reported. A CubeSat model development kit is planned; reproducibility is constrained by proprietary COTS tools and vendor-supported integration.

RQ1: RAX shows a CubeSat mission can be modeled with SysML BDD/IBD, parametric, state-machine, activity, and generic requirements artifacts spanning mission, flight, ground, operations, environment, and selected subsystems.
Logical/physical separation and modular subsystem decomposition allow useful operations-level modeling without full hardware detail; however mission/tool knowledge remains important.
Reusable mechanisms include CubeSat meta-model/framework/template concepts, acausal parametrics, modular workflows, and analysis-driven model minimization.
RQ2: Best-supported outcome is integrability/interoperability of a SysML-centered toolchain for SNR, power, and behavior analyses.
Power-related outcomes include dynamic energy/data scenario simulation, requirement-compliance checks, and violation metrics, but no validated EPS reliability/reproducibility improvement is reported.
Claims about reuse, communication, full lifecycle continuity, and operational feedback are mainly prospective or qualitatively supported.
RQ3: Pre-physical verification is represented in principle through executable power/SNR parametric models, requirements-compliance checks, simulations, and virtual integration.
Behavioral V&V is addressed via CST execution of state/activity models for flight-ground interfaces and command dispatch.
No formal EPS verification matrix/procedure, hardware-in-the-loop/flat-sat, or flight-data validation of EPS model results is reported.

SLIM connects SysML elements to PLM artifacts in Windchill/Teamcenter, generates PLM part structures from SysML and SysML block structures from PLM payload parts, saves connections, manages versions, and is intended to synchronize requirements/parts/MySQL data across repositories.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_lifecycle_continuity: The paper's continuity mechanism is a 'unique model' or blueprint linking systems-level SysML to domain-specific PLM/BOM/CAD/CAE/analysis artifacts and versions across formulation, design, manufacturing, and operations.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: SysML-generated Windchill BOMs provide a starting point for mechanical/electrical designers and part decomposition; no hardware integration/test readiness evidence is reported.

availability_reproducibility.models_or_data_available: RAX CubeSat model and manual are reported as being made available to the academic community; conclusion says framework model and tool instructions are available to the CubeSat community.
availability_reproducibility.reproducibility_assessment: partial; named COTS toolchain and manual sections support assessment, but complete model package, versions, licenses, and access URL are not in the paper.

eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_represented: The paper reports requirements for battery capacity and margin alongside data collection, storage, and download. Power collection and management subsystems are modeled to demonstrate interdependencies among requirements. The architecture includes EPS generation/storage/distribution and power overhead per component/interface/task.
eps_verification_specific.requirements_linkage: Power/data requirements are linked to mission scenarios and trade studies in the integrated model; detailed requirement IDs/tables/matrices are not shown.
eps_verification_specific.evidence_integrated_into_model: The verification mechanism is integrated into the system-level SysML/analysis model rather than described as a separate test procedure: Cameo executes mission scenarios with analysis models, enabling requirements verification and trades on solar panel/battery sizes.
eps_verification_specific.eps_scope_caution: EPS is covered as a power-budget/electrical-architecture aspect within a system-level CubeSat enterprise model, not as a dedicated EPS MBSE verification-method paper.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: The highest supported IVV integration level is simulation-in-the-loop: SysML is connected with analytical/simulation tools and executed for mission-scenario requirements verification, including battery capacity/margin and solar-panel/battery trades. The paper does not support SIL/HIL, physical integration/test, or model-contained EPS test procedures.

RQ1: A reusable SysML CubeSat architecture framework can represent mission definition, requirements flow-down, logical/physical flight and ground systems, subsystems, components, interfaces, tasks, operating modes, CONOPS, and enterprise concerns.

The framework functions as a CubeSat systems-engineering kit/library and model/manual starting point, but it does not explicitly solve modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge beyond reuse of common elements and CONOPS-driven decomposition.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include traceability, reuse/reproducibility, communication, lifecycle continuity, automation, decision support, and some reliability/robustness/risk-reduction expectations.

Power/EPS-related evidence consists of system-level power collection/management, battery margin, solar-panel/battery trade studies, and power budgets; outcomes are not EPS-specific and lack quantitative reliability/reproducibility/integration metrics.
RQ3: The paper reports pre-physical simulation-in-the-loop/requirements-in-the-loop verification for mission scenarios, including solar-panel/battery parameters and battery-capacity/margin requirements.
It does not present formal EPS verification procedures, test cases, verification matrices, SIL/HIL/flat-sat links, or physical test/flight validation.

Ground-system functional-flow transformation into SysML is current/future work.

CubeSat cost estimation is challenged by unpaid/volunteer labor, dynamic requirements/architecture, lack of standards, small-mass database issues, and proprietary/unknown launch costs.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: At system level, the paper shows formal/model-based verification through PVS proof obligations and type-correctness checks tied to abstraction-level consistency and traceability. RQ1: Provides a general PNSat system-level modeling concept using abstraction levels linking natural-language requirements, logical requirements, models, parametric simulations, and behavior simulations.
Supports the idea of starting with broad mission objectives and refining through mission characteristics/concept selection to domain design, but no EPS general model is provided.
Generality is methodological: SysML common language, proposed profiles/stereotypes, SMAD-derived workflow, and formal refinement/traceability.
RQ2: Claims reliability/mission-assurance value through formal specifications, PVS checking, consistency, traceability, and correct-by-construction design.
Claims integrability and communication benefits through common SysML semantics, formal methods, and virtual testing.
Reproducibility is weakly supported through claims about peer-review/archival formal specifications; no available artifacts or EPS-specific evidence.
RQ3: Pre-physical verification is described at system level via requirements-in-the-loop formalization, PVS type checking/proof obligations, parametric/behavior simulations, and refinement traceability.
The verification example is a railway crossing, not EPS, so it is only analogical support for EPS verification integration.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Formal methods cannot fix incorrect design assumptions.
Formal methods can be difficult to comprehend/use and are not a panacea; costs can be prohibitive in some areas.
Implementation of the traceability check integrated with RFD is future work.
Manual traceability link capture grows exponentially with software system size/complexity.
Strict refinement constraints may limit design space.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS elements, power budgets, battery/solar/power-conditioning models, or EPS verification artifacts.
No concrete PNSat/CubeSat case study, orbit, payload, project maturity, integration test, operation, or flight evidence.
No quantitative metrics or baseline comparison for reliability, integration, effort, schedule, cost, or redesign claims.
No available SysML profile, model repository, PVS proof files, proof scripts, or automated SysML-PVS integration.
Only worked example is a railway crossing, limiting direct nanosatellite/EPS evidence.

evidence.quote: The CSRM is a SysML compliant and platform-independent model that provides building blocks that can be specialized to support CubeSat mission design.

The CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) is a representation of the logical architecture of a CubeSat System, intended to be used by system architects and engineers as a starting point as they develop the logical architecture of the Space and Ground components of the CubeSat mission of interest to them.
The CSRM provides a library of model elements but does not dictate what model elements and relationships to use.

The CSRM provides a CubeSat logical space-ground architecture. The logical components are abstractions of the physical components that perform the system functionality without imposing implementation constraints.
The CubeSat subsystems are generically and loosely defined as a starting point for the mission specific CubeSat team.

RQ1: The paper provides a CubeSat mission/system reference model in SysML organized around stakeholders, requirements, behaviors, architecture, technical measures, and V&V.
Generalization is achieved through a platform-independent reference model, reusable library of elements, generic/loosely defined subsystems, and methodology-agnostic population guidance.
EPS is not modeled in detail; power appears as a generic subsystem and in lineage-level power trade-study history.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include reuse, quality enhancement, development-time reduction, common baseline comparison, institutional knowledge transfer, traceability, and standards/reusable-library potential.

Evidence is mostly qualitative: formal review, university use, model-structure figures, and historical trade-study mentions; no quantitative EPS reliability/reproducibility/integrability evidence is reported.
The strongest synthesis-relevant evidence is structural traceability and reported vetting/use, not measured project performance.
RQ3: The CSRM includes validation and verification packages and activity elements that can capture plans, procedures, execution notes/results/status and link to requirements, objectives, and technical measures.
Pre-physical verification is conceptual/model-structural and generic rather than an EPS-specific procedure or executable check in this paper.
No EPS test procedures, verification matrix, SIL/HIL, hardware integration, or flight evidence are presented.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The CSRM is targeted especially at university CubeSat mission architecture teams and is not methodology-specific.
Teams determine which model elements and relationships to use and may modify the containment tree to fit their methodology.
Feedback from university teams will be evaluated for inclusion, including value-added elements not currently in the CSRM, portions that do not function as intended, and new capabilities.
Dissemination/control/update processes and formats for a possible OMG specification have yet to be worked out.
Expansion from CubeSats to broader satellite classes is future work.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No dedicated EPS model, EPS requirement set, power modes/loads, EPS verification procedure, or EPS test evidence.
Claims about development time, quality, economies, reuse, and common baseline lack metrics, baselines, and effect sizes.
Model file, version, license, repository, current tool instance, and exchange formats are not provided.
Vetting and university-use claims lack evaluation criteria, detailed feedback, and outcome data.
No hardware/software integration, operational, or flight evidence for CSRM benefits.
Lineage overlap with prior RAX/CSRM publications should be accounted for in synthesis.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Manual point-design mission analysis and isolated discipline trades are slow and may miss near-optimal CubeSat mission designs; the paper proposes a rapid model-based architecture linking decision variables to cost/performance metrics.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Mission-level CubeSat architecture with trajectory, space segment, launch segment, ground segment, and performance modules at conceptual analytical/parametric fidelity.
minimal_or_excluded_modeling: No detailed numerical orbit propagation for most visibility calculations.
Only circular orbits and long-term averages are considered for trajectory variables.
No detailed EPS dynamic behavior, fault protection, software, hardware integration, or flight operations model.

Complete novel mission design is out of scope.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Mission requirements, objectives, decision-variable bounds, payload/communication demands, OTS CubeSat subsystem data, and analytical equations/assumptions for orbit visibility, power sizing, cost, lifetime, and de-orbit behavior.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.limited_behavioral_knowledge_handling: Uses analytical approximations, long-term averages, conservative/safety factors, OTS databases, simplified duty-cycle assumptions, and penalty functions to screen many designs without detailed behavior models.
direct_quotes: Section 1.1: "a baseline structure can be maintained with modifications of the inputs and requirements made for each use case."
Abstract: "This work presents an architecture that identifies trends between conflicting objectives... and decision variables..."

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The reusable contribution is a baseline CubeSat mission-design architecture/workflow and guidance, not a fully mission-agnostic or interface-focused model. The paper explicitly says the architecture cannot be completely generalized but can be maintained as a baseline with modified inputs/requirements. Its generality also depends on high-level analytical abstractions and deliberate avoidance of detailed/numerical dynamic behavior. The current 'specific-mission model with reusable method only' is overstated because the paper demonstrates two generic use cases rather than one specific mission model.

evidence.quote: Since each space mission is unique, the model architecture introduced here cannot be completely generalized, however a baseline structure can be maintained with modifications of the inputs and requirements made for each use case.

RQ1: A baseline CubeSat mission architecture can model trajectory, space, launch, ground, and performance disciplines with mission-specific inputs and requirements.
EPS relevance is power-budget/electrical-architecture only: subsystem loads, battery sizing, solar-array sizing, and feasibility/cost contributions.
Limited behavioral knowledge is handled through analytical approximations, long-term averages, OTS component data, conservative factors, and penalty functions.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include rapid trade-space exploration, Pareto-set decision support, broader solution-space coverage, inter-disciplinary integration, and possible robustness/lifecycle continuity.
Best evidence is executable case-study results and a runtime metric; reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes are not proven with independent validation, reuse, or flight/test evidence.
Reproducibility is partial because equations/settings are reported but model/data/code are not available.
RQ3: Pre-physical checks include power, battery, solar-array, volume, lifetime, de-orbit, and constraint/penalty screening.
No formal EPS verification procedure, verification matrix, test cases/procedures, model checking, SIL/HIL, or hardware integration/test evidence is reported.
The paper's 'verifies the model architecture' statement is a simple case-study sanity check, not EPS IVV.

RQ1.rationale: Directly describes a general CubeSat/nanosatellite system reference model with reusable and loosely defined mission, architecture, requirement, use-case, and technical-measure packages.

RQ2.rationale: Provides system-level reuse, traceability, reproducibility, and interoperability claims attributed to MBSE/CRM; EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes are not demonstrated.

RQ3.rationale: Generic verify properties, technical-measure parametrics, prior trade studies, and CRM validation are reported, but no EPS-specific verification procedures are integrated into an EPS model.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: High failure rates and intuition-based design in university-class CubeSats motivate rigorous systems engineering and a reusable CRM for instruction and mission-specific design/build.
modeling_scope: stakeholders, stakeholder concerns, needs, objectives, constraints, and requirements
space segment, ground segment, CubeSat subsystems, ground subsystems, and representative components
logical architecture and physical architecture transition
technical measures (MOE/MOP/TPM) and parametric performance analysis
generic verification properties and CRM validation strategy
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: Generic CubeSat mission enterprise with space and ground segments, generic/loose subsystem definitions, representative subsystem components, external environment/constraints, provided services, and mission-specific tailoring to physical architecture. The CRM deliberately avoids imposing implementation constraints.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: The CRM is methodology-agnostic and provides a library rather than prescribing all model elements/relationships. Power, weight, and cost parametrics are next steps, and the current paper does not provide EPS-specific verification artifacts, full model files, or complete validation results.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The mission team chooses Fundamental, Representative, or Detailed package levels depending on experience with space-ground systems, MBSE, and SysML; the paper assumes access to a graphical SysML tool and some systems engineering/modeling competence.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: Generic and loosely defined subsystems, use-case narratives, representative components, table-based population, and reference information allow teams to incrementally add mission-specific behavior and physical components.

block definition diagrams and structure tables

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper explicitly presents the CRM as a reusable CubeSat community starting point and OMG specification candidate, not just a high-level one-off model. Reuse is supported by a template/reference model, model-element library, stereotypes/profiles, generic logical architecture, loose subsystem definitions, table-based population workflow, and user guidance. Do not add interface-focused model or specific-mission model with reusable method only.

evidence.quote: Because the initial model was RAX-centric and not suitable for reuse... Develop a CubeSat Reference Model (CRM) that a CubeSat team can use as a starting point for its mission
The CRM provides a library of model elements but does not dictate what model elements and relationships to use.
The CRM provides a CubeSat logical architecture. The logical components are abstractions of the physical components... without imposing implementation constraints.
The CubeSat and Ground subsystems are generically and loosely defined as a starting point for the mission-specific CubeSat team.
It is a template model that provides building blocks that can be specialized to support MBSE CubeSat design.
A use case can be described in a Use Case Description document... and then, if warranted, detailed in a SysML model.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The CSRM is a reusable CubeSat reference/logical architecture intended as a starting point for mission teams, not a single mission-specific model. It is mission-agnostic because teams populate mission-specific stakeholders, requirements, behaviors, and measures. It uses high-level logical abstractions and does not impose physical implementation constraints. The paper also supports a non-detailed/descriptive behavior interpretation because the model is not pre-populated with behaviors and the authors state that dynamic/performance analysis requires external mission models and further research. Do not add interface-focused model or specific-mission model with reusable method only.

evidence.quote: The International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) Space System Working Group (SSWG) has created the CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM), a representation of the logical architecture of a CubeSat system, intended to be used by system architects and engineers as a starting point as they develop the physical architecture of the Space and Ground segments of the CubeSat mission of interest to them.
The logical components are abstractions of the physical components that perform the system functionality without imposing implementation constraints.

The CSRM is a repository for systems engineering artifacts. However, it is not pre-populated with specific stakeholders, technical measures, behaviors, and requirements. That is the job of the CubeSat mission development team, specific to their needs and objectives.
A mission-specific CubeSat team downloads the CSRM specification and files from OMG for import it into their own graphical modeling tool.

While these products enable a complete description of a mission from multiple perspectives, they do not enable detailed analysis of the performance of that mission...Proper analysis requires definition and analysis of external mission models.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Many CubeSat teams are first-time developers with small budgets and limited systems-engineering capacity. The project aims to demonstrate MBSE/OOSEM and provide a reusable CubeSat Reference Model for mission-specific models and concept lifecycle studies.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: System boundary is a CubeSat mission including space and ground systems. Abstraction is primarily logical architecture, stakeholder/MOE structure, operations phases, subsystem-level power/weight parameters, and concept trade-study behavior; mission teams create the physical architecture.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Detailed physical architecture, component implementation, detailed EPS behavior, executable model files, concrete trace matrices, and validation results are not included. Example mission-specific model validation is future work.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Not explicitly characterized. Users must supply mission-specific stakeholders, objectives, model elements, parameters, and simulation interfaces; the reference model reduces start-up burden by supplying logical elements, nomenclature, and workflow.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: The model supplies reusable logical building blocks and lifecycle-phase subsets, so teams can gradually populate mission-specific stakeholders, measures, parameters, and behavior diagrams rather than starting from a blank model.
model_artifacts_used: SysML blocks, actors, flows, signals, ports, and block properties
logical space and ground subsystem elements
mission-specific model derived from the reference model

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper directly supports a reusable CubeSat reference-model/template, mission-agnostic logical architecture, component library, and concept-trade workflow. It also supports high-level abstraction through logical components without implementation constraints and interface-focused modeling through interface management, data/information flows, and COTS simulation interfaces. Do not code specific-mission model with reusable method only because the current contribution is explicitly generic, not only a specific mission case. Do not code low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model: although the current model is high-level/logical, the paper does not present non-detailed behavior itself as the reuse mechanism and also discusses behavior/state/activity diagrams.

evidence.quote: Provide a CubeSat Reference Model that CubeSat teams can use as starting point for their mission-specific CubeSat model.
The purpose of the CubeSat Reference Model is to provide a logical architecture, which serves as a guide and provide the building blocks for any kind of CubeSat mission.
The logical components are abstractions of the physical components that perform the system functionality without imposing implementation constraints.
The system model also integrates other discipline specific engineering models and simulations.

RQ1: Strong system-level evidence for a general CubeSat SysML/OOSEM reference model with logical architecture, stakeholders, lifecycle stages, operations phases, and reusable subsystem building blocks.
Limited EPS-specific generality: Power subsystem and power/weight parametrics are present, but detailed EPS behavior/requirements are not developed.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include reuse, reduced systems-engineering burden, checklist completeness, uniformity/consistency, single-source repository, and concept trade decision support.
Outcome evidence is weak: no measured reliability/reproducibility/integrability effects, no baseline, and no current quantitative results.
RQ3: Pre-physical verification appears only as conceptual trade-study requirements verification and simulation-in-the-loop parameter exchange with STK.
No EPS-specific verification procedure, test cases/procedures, verification matrix, SIL/HIL, or automated checks are provided.

RQ1.rationale: Central contribution is a general, reusable framework/repository for initial nanosatellite mission/project modeling and design with limited resources.

RQ2.rationale: Reliability, traceability, communication, and project-management outcomes are claimed, and power-system artifacts are shown, but EPS-specific outcome evidence is limited and unquantified.

RQ3.rationale: Requirements-linked verification artifacts and a power-bus activation state machine are integrated in SysML, but no full EPS verification procedure or physical/electrical test evidence is reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Builds on INCOSE SSWG CubeSat MBSE reference-model papers and Guo et al. DelFFi nanosatellite MBSE work, but applies a distinct ECSS/NASA-tailored framework to MASAT1. Treat as related background lineage, not a duplicate result.

mission_platform.size_form_factor: 1U CubeSat design is referenced in requirements; MASAT1 is described as a nanosatellite/CubeSat project.
mission_platform.mission_domain: Academic technology acquisition/demonstration: ready-to-fly CubeSat system with efficient power management, low-cost mission-control ground station, and FPGA-based secondary onboard computer payload.
mission_platform.orbit_or_environment: Low Earth Orbit context is stated for university nanosatellite missions generally; MASAT1 orbit details are not specified.
mission_platform.organization_type: University/academic project at University of Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah, Fez, Morocco, with CNRST as main customer and university professors as stakeholders.
mission_platform.project_maturity: First MASAT1 university nanosatellite project; paper applies MBSE mainly to preparation, mission analysis, and PBS/product-tree modeling rather than reporting flight/operation.

study_context_population.context_notes: The paper is useful for synthesis as an academic nanosatellite framework with substantial system-level and power-subsystem modeling examples, but it is not an EPS-only or flight-validated study.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Improve the success of academic/university nanosatellite missions and help limited-resource student teams start project management and design effectively, because DBSE/ECSS practices are over-specified for nanosatellite projects and early management guidance is sparse.

system_boundary_and_level_of_abstraction.included: Nanosatellite project framework views; mission analysis, formal design, production/integration, deployment/operation; MASAT1 space and ground segments; platform subsystems and payload; power system detailed as requirements/components/interfaces; ConOps/LEOP behavior.
system_boundary_and_level_of_abstraction.detailed: Mission-analysis process, requirements categories/identifiers, product tree/PBS, requirements tables/matrices, BDD/IBD for structure/interfaces, ConOps state machine, LEOP activity and power bus activation behavior.
system_boundary_and_level_of_abstraction.minimal_or_excluded: Executable SysML, external MATLAB/STK simulations, GUI, quantitative analysis results, complete formal design/production/operation model, and physical integration/flight evidence are not implemented in the paper.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.prior_behavioral_domain_knowledge: The method reduces the need for mature technical design knowledge at project start by guiding stakeholders through needs, ConOps, requirements, functional breakdown, and standard-derived project structures. It still requires ECSS/NASA systems-engineering knowledge, SysML tooling, mission objectives, stakeholder inputs, and subsystem/component knowledge for detailed models.
model_artifacts_used: Requirements diagrams and generated requirements tables
Mission Satisfy Requirement Matrix and Satisfied By/Verified By columns
Package diagrams for lifecycle, mission analysis, and PBS organization
Product Tree and product breakdown structure (PBS)
Work breakdown structure (WBS) and cost breakdown structure (CBS) as derived deliverables
Block definition diagrams for space segment and power system
Internal block diagrams for space-segment data flows and power-system interconnections
State machine diagrams for CubeSat ConOps and Bus System Activation
Activity diagrams for mission definition, functional breakdown, and LEOP flow
Parametric package/parameters and analysis concept; no reported executed parametric result
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.reuse_availability_notes: The framework is intended as a reusable repository/template for university teams, but no model files, open package, scripts, or repository URL are reported.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper claims a reusable framework/repository/reference model for university CubeSat/nanosatellite teams, expressed through abstract lifecycle/views and process flows. It also includes generic subsystem/interface architecture and explicitly generalizes beyond MASAT1 in the ConOps. Do not code low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model from absence of executable detail alone.

evidence.quote: The aim of using MBSE for a nanosatellite project is to create a model framework or repository that can be used by university teams (with limited resources) wishing to design CubeSat or Nanosatellite projects.

MBSE approach can be used to create a PBS model repository that can be used by university teams designing nanosatellite projects, for requirements, design, analysis verification, and validation activities. Choosing to use package diagrams at this level of abstract modeling helps stakeholders understand the structure of the model.

Although MASAT1 mission uses passive attitude control, an attitude control mode has been included in ConOps to generalize the model proposed in this paper.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_and_gates: Needs definition -> MCR; requirements definition -> MRR; functional breakdown -> SDR/PBS/WBS/CBS; formal design -> PDR/CDR; production/integration -> SAR/PRR; deployment/operations -> ORR/DR. The mapping is explicit in lifecycle/process diagrams but detailed evidence is strongest for Mission Analysis and PBS.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.tailoring_notes: Tailored for student-driven university nanosatellites without industrial customer-supplier arrangements; business-agreement structure is neglected, costs/schedules are derived from product tree/WBS, and standards are simplified.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.adoption_guidance_notes: The paper gives process flows and model artifacts but not a complete implementation manual, role matrix, model repository, or toolchain setup package.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_and_data_flow: Primary implementation is a SysML model in No Magic MagicDraw with Cameo Simulation Toolkit plugin. The model is organized into requirements, structure, behavior, verification, parametric, and launch-operation packages. No implemented external data flow to MATLAB/STK is described; those integrations are future work.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity: Within SysML, requirement identifiers, satisfy/verify links, BDD/IBD elements, activity/state behavior, and lifecycle views provide semantic continuity from mission objectives to design and verification artifacts. Cross-tool syntax/semantic continuity is not demonstrated.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Conceptual lifecycle links to Phase B test hardware/software and Phase C flight hardware/software integration are modeled; no generated code, software integration, HIL/SIL, testbed, or hardware interface implementation is reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: Tools and diagram types are named and many figures are shown. The model/package is not available in the paper; no exchange format, script, API, repository, or data package is reported.

eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_represented: Power system requirements include margin, PV cell degradation/performance, topology, battery recharge, power distribution to static/dynamic loads, protection against failure propagation, structural electrical constraints, and degradation factors. Operational requirements such as modes transition and antenna deployment under optimal power supply are satisfied by the Power System in trace tables.
eps_verification_specific.evidence_integrated_not_separate: The SysML requirements table embeds Satisfied By and Verified By columns; requirement 100.1.6 is satisfied by Power System and verified by LEOP Flow/Bus System Activation. The requirements matrix and behavior/state diagrams are within the SysML/PBS model organization, not merely separate narrative documents.
eps_verification_specific.notes: EPS coverage is architectural and requirement/behavior linkage oriented. No power-budget calculation, executed simulation, test procedure details, acceptance results, SIL/HIL link, or physical EPS verification evidence is reported.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: The SysML requirements table/matrix links requirements to satisfying model elements and verifying behavior/test artifacts, including a Power System satisfy link and Bus System Activation verification. No executable checks, simulation-in-the-loop, SIL/HIL, or physical verification evidence is reported.

evidence.quote: These tables describe the requirements and their relationship to other SysML design elements to facilitate requirements traceability, satisfaction, and verification.
The "Satisfied By" column shows the model elements that fulfill the requirement. For example, the "Power System" subsystem must satisfy operational requirement 100.1.6.

The 'Verified By' column shows the specific test cases that determine how the system meets the requirement. For example, the "Bus System Activation" activity diagram ... is used to verify operational requirement 100.1.6.

direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi: Abstract: "This paper aims to contribute to research efforts to improve the success of university nanosatellite missions using Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) to facilitate the initial project management and design phases."

Section 2: "The aim of using MBSE for a nanosatellite project is to create a model framework or repository that can be used by university teams (with limited resources) wishing to design CubeSat or Nanosatellite projects. This type of formal modeling application will guide them through the entire nanosatellite mission design and management process (mission analysis, system design verification, and validation)."

Section 3.2: academic nanosatellite specificities allow simplifying the structure: requirements are derived from mission objectives; budget is allocated to hardware/software; "schedule and Coast Breakdown Structure can be directly derived from the Product Tree"; "students-driven projects" have changing personnel and "Business Agreement Structure can be neglected."

Section 5.1: "requirements tables were generated ... These tables describe the requirements and their relationship to other SysML design elements to facilitate requirements traceability, satisfaction, and verification."

Section 5.1/Fig. 15: "The "Satisfied By" column shows the model elements that fulfill the requirement. For example, the "Power System" subsystem must satisfy operational requirement 100.1.6."; "The 'Verified By' column shows the specific test cases that determine how the system meets the requirement ... "Bus System Activation" activity diagram ... is used to verify operational requirement 100.1.6."

Section 5.3: "The LEOP flow activity diagram is also a way to "verify" functional or operational requirements, such as the Bus System Activation state machine (Fig. 23), which verifies operational requirements 100.1.6."

Conclusion: "The next step of this work is to improve the viability and practicality of the product breakdown structure model by integrating external analysis and simulation tools such as MATLAB and STK. The aim is to develop an executable SysML model with a graphical user interface to provide insight into how nanosatellites work."

RQ1.rationale: Directly addresses generic CubeSat preliminary-design modeling with known unknowns, SysML artifacts, dependency graphs, DSMs, and reusable scripts/workflow. EPS/power is included as a budget but not a full EPS model.

RQ2.rationale: Claims traceability, reuse, communication, consistency, cost/time, automation, and decision support from MBSE/Nanospace, but evidence is mostly conceptual or from one case and not EPS-specific.

RQ3.rationale: Includes pre-physical requirement/constraint checking for power and system design, but no formal EPS verification procedure model, verification matrix, or test-procedure integration.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of the Nanospace open-source CubeSat concurrent-design toolchain lineage (Gateau et al. 2021) and related DSM/MB2DM work. The CREME use case builds on ISAE-SUPAERO/ONERA CubeSat experience and references EyeSat/EntrySat heritage.

study_context_population.mission_platform: CREME CubeSat Radiation Environment Monitoring Experiment, a nanosatellite/CubeSat mission for LEO radiation-environment measurement; example iterations consider 2U feasibility and then 3U sizing.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: CubeSat; paper defines 1U as 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm up to 2 kg; CREME payload is 1.5U, initial spacecraft at least 2U, later 3U scenario.
study_context_population.mission_name: CREME
study_context_population.mission_domain: Space-weather/radiation environment monitoring in Low Earth Orbit; charged-particle detector payload.
study_context_population.organization_type: Academic/university-led platform at ISAE-SUPAERO with ONERA payload and CSUT exploitation perspective; open-source/educational tool context.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Approved by Occitanie region and started late 2020; paper uses a simplified subset of requirements/constraints during preliminary design.
study_context_population.eps_relevance_notes: Power subsystem is treated through solar-panel generation, battery capacity/DoD, payload/platform loads, eclipse duration, and power-budget plots; not a complete EPS architecture/verification model.
context_quotes: 'Nanospace is a web application dedicated to facilitate concurrent engineering during the preliminary design phase of CubeSats.'
'The CubeSat Radiation Environment Monitoring Experiment (CREME) project ... objective is to measure the radiation environment in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).'
'Telecommunication and power are traditionally the most critical subsystems to ensure mission survival.'

stated_objective_pain_point: Integrate MBSE with the open-source Nanospace concurrent-design environment for CubeSat preliminary design.
Improve communication and system-level coordination among experts; reduce manual systems-engineer monitoring of process order, consistency, and up-to-date shared data.
Capture CubeSat parameter dependencies so DSMs/dependency graphs can guide iterations and change propagation.
Archive/reuse CubeSat design knowledge from prior missions and support faster architecture inspection.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Simplified preliminary-design CubeSat model covering mission/orbit, telecommunications, on-board computing/data storage, energy and power, structure, payload, and ground segment parameters. The paper uses subset requirements/constraints and preliminary estimates, assumes circular orbit and sun-pointing when not in eclipse, omits mission modes, and excludes ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations from the example.
deliberately_minimal_or_excluded: Only subset of CREME requirements/constraints due to space constraints.
Mission modes not discussed; authors state concept can be extended to include them.
ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations omitted from example but described as fundamental for real missions.
Initial power/platform values use rough expert estimates and worst-case scenario assumptions.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Method still relies on expert starting values and experience for known unknowns, flight-proven component preferences, margins, and trade-off decisions. MBSE is proposed to capture/reuse this knowledge through dependencies and models but does not eliminate expert judgment.
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only
key_quotes: 'MBSE can be used to capture the system dependencies represented in Figs.1 and 2, allowing to reuse knowledge from previous CubeSat missions.'
'From these system models, using a dedicated algorithm it is possible to generate Design Structure Matrices (DSMs) from a SysML model.'
'The models contain the functions related to the CubeSat, the space environment, the launch segment, the ground segment, the customer and the legislative and regulatory institutions.'

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper supports reuse mainly as a transferable preliminary-design method around Nanospace, scripts, SysML-to-DSM transformation, and dependency/parameter abstractions. The CREME demonstration is still a specific use case, so mission-agnostic architecture should not be coded. v1.1 labels are supported because the model is high-level, parameter/interface/dependency-focused, and deliberately omits detailed behavior/modes/domains, while claiming the diagrams can be reshaped for new missions.

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper claims a reusable generic CubeSat SysML formalization, not merely a TWC-specific model. Mission-agnostic architecture is supported within the CubeSat/mostly LEO preliminary-design scope, but interface-focused model and specific-mission model with reusable method only should not be coded.

evidence.quote: How to formalize a CubeSat model that is general enough to be reusable across different mission designs, yet detailed enough for a comprehensive representation of the systems?

This paper aims to formalize a generalized SysML CubeSat model that has been enhanced through the use of UML stereotypes for data characterization at any design stage and is capable of being linked with any set of open source simulation tools

The main discrepancies between the various OMs can thus be reduced, at the level of detail desired, to when a specific OM is activated and which subsystems are active in that mode. This can be further simplified to the differences in average power consumption and data rate.
the parser itself, being developed to work with the proposed set of stereotypes, is reusable with any model compliant with the proposed formalization.
once the proposed set of stereotypes are integrated within the model, it becomes possible to reuse them for different designs by only varying the introduced data.

RQ1: High relevance: presents a reusable CubeSat SysML/UML stereotype profile and model/parser workflow for preliminary design with limited detailed behavior.
Generalizes nominal operating modes via activation criteria, priority, power consumption, data rates, and metadata.
Supports early-stage abstraction through SystemMain aggregate values and computeMass/computeCons flags.
RQ2: Partial relevance: strongest claims are integrability/interoperability, reproducibility, generality/reuse, automation, and lifecycle continuity from model-to-tool data flow.
EPS/power-budget evidence exists through battery/solar/load/mode parameters and generated power budget, but outcomes are not evaluated against a baseline.
Reliability/mission-assurance benefits are mostly background/implicit; no measured reliability outcome is reported.
RQ3: Partial relevance: EPS requirements and pre-physical power-budget simulations are present.
No formal EPS verification procedures, verification matrices, test cases, acceptance-criteria checks, SIL/HIL, or automated V&V artifacts are integrated into the model.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Gaphor-specific parser restricts immediate applicability to other SysML tools.
Model file formats are not fully interoperable by default across modeling tools.
OM generalization focuses on LEO and excludes non-nominal/EOP modes such as detumbling, calibration, and safe modes.
Generic framework may require customization for specific mission requirements.
Future work needed for complex subsystems such as AOCS/propulsion, Delta-V/propellant budgets, broader mission types, parser output selection, and database formats such as SQL.
NSS tool approximations are acknowledged; Table 9 sets eccentricity to zero due to tool limits.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No baseline/comparator or quantitative evaluation of MBSE benefits such as cost, schedule, effort, errors, or integration failures.
No independent validation, user/stakeholder evaluation, repeated reuse, physical integration/test, or flight evidence.
No formal requirements traceability to architecture/verification artifacts beyond generated requirements list and dependency graph.
No explicit model governance/change-control strategy or ROI evidence.
EPS relevance is primarily power-budget analysis, not EPS-specific V&V modeling.
direct_evidence_quotes_for_classificatio: Abstract: "This paper focuses on formalizing a CubeSat model for use across various stages of the PD phase."
Section 1: "The novelty of this approach resides in its capability to include relevant design parameters within a CubeSat model... automatically extracted through a dedicated parser..."
Section 3.3: "the parser itself... is reusable with any model compliant with the proposed formalization."
Section 4: "The parser allows the parsing process to be inverted to facilitate automatic updates to model files after analysis or optimization tasks."

Section 5: "as a drawback, the current state-of-the-art model parser does not allow data to be automatically extracted from models developed with tools other than Gaphor without modifying the source code."
Section 6: "A proof of concept is presented with the SysML model of the TWC mission... successfully generating power and data budgets."
synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Treat as an extension of the Nanostar/Nanospace open-source CubeSat CE/PD lineage. Do not double-count outcomes already claimed in prior NSS papers unless this paper adds SysML/UML stereotype formalization, Gaphor XML parser, dependency graph, or public repository evidence.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: Clear full text and detailed methods/limitations; controlled coding is high confidence for MBSE/model/toolchain/context and high-confidence absence for V&V/ROI/governance. Some confidence is medium for broad claims because the paper uses conceptual language without empirical evaluation.

study_context_population.mission_platform: Generic CubeSat/CubeSat Enterprise reference model; RAX three-unit CubeSat and hypothetical FireSat are lineage examples.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: CubeSat standardized unit cube of 10 cm on a side and about 1 kg per cube; typically one to three units, with some up to six units; RAX is described as a three-unit CubeSat.
study_context_population.mission_name: CubeSat Reference Model; prior examples include Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) and hypothetical FireSat.
study_context_population.mission_domain: CubeSat space systems including space segment, ground segment, launch/deployment services, external environment, external constraints/regulations, and mission operations.
study_context_population.organization_type: INCOSE Space Systems Working Group Challenge Team spanning students, professors, engineers, software developers, government, industry, academia, and modeling/simulation tool providers.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Develop and distribute a CubeSat SysML reference model that captures basic CubeSat project features, provides a framework/checklist for future CubeSat developers, reduces small-team systems-engineering burden, and promotes uniformity and consistency.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Generic logical CubeSat Enterprise architecture including CubeSat Space System, CubeSat Ground System, stakeholders, external environment/constraints, and provided services. Decomposition reaches logical subsystem level rather than mission-specific physical component design.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.deliberately_minimal_or_excluded: GPS and relay satellites are outside Space/Ground Systems unless developed by the CubeSat project; external transport/launch/deploy and ground-station services are treated as provided services; detailed model-element refinement, mission-specific physical architecture, correctness verification, and release are future work.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_or_domain_know: No explicit prerequisite behavioral knowledge is stated. The method relies on SysML/OOSEM, CubeSat standards/specifications, stakeholder needs, regulatory constraints, and user tailoring of logical elements to mission-specific physical architectures.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: The reference model starts with stakeholder needs, requirements, constraints, lifecycle/operations phases, and a reusable logical architecture so users can tailor it before detailed physical design; behavior and power/communication simulations are shown as prior extensions rather than required for every element.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_and_lifecycle_g: MBSE is mapped to requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation beginning in conceptual design and continuing through later lifecycle phases. The model supports concept, development/production, operations, retirement, pre-launch integration/test, launch, early orbit checkout, and full mission operations. Named SRR/PDR/CDR gates are not reported.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The paper connects SysML/OOSEM modeling with requirements/traceability, behavior/constraint execution, prior simulation/trade studies, lifecycle/operations coverage, and distribution/interoperability options, but does not evidence a full integrated digital engineering environment spanning verified downstream hardware/software integration.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.tailoring_rationale_text: The reference model is positioned for small CubeSat teams and project-specific tailoring; distribution channels/tools and copyright/licensing constraints shape adoption.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_and_data_flow: A central SysML reference model contains requirements, interfaces, structure, behavior, parametric views, stakeholders, measures, and logical architectures. Documents/views can be generated from model content; prior behavior/constraint models interface with simulations/trade studies; distribution sends model files/walkthroughs to users and feedback back to SSWG.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity_evidence: SysML supplies common modeling semantics and XMI is listed as an exchange option; the paper does not report a validated semantic-continuity test across tools for the current reference model.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: The model claims support for pre-launch integration/test and physical-system development from the model, and includes launch service integration roles/constraints, but no software/hardware integration result is reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: Prospective: model files and walkthrough videos are planned for distribution; current paper does not report completed public availability or reproducible package access.

eps_verification_specific.eps_elements_text: Prior phases modeled a power subsystem accounting for solar energy collection/storage and subsystem power consumption; trade studies varied solar panel area and maximum battery capacity to assess on-board energy level.
eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_represented: EPS-specific requirements are not separately detailed. The Cal Poly SysML requirements model includes electrical and testing requirements at a general CubeSat specification level.
eps_verification_specific.evidence_verification_integrated_in_mode: No EPS-specific verification procedure/model is reported. Generic MBSE V&V support, testing requirements, tester stakeholder definitions, traceability, and future model-correctness verification are present but insufficient for RQ3.
eps_verification_specific.integration_test_readiness: Generic pre-launch integration/test and launch/deployment interface coverage is stated; no EPS-specific hardware/software integration, flat-sat/testbed, environmental test, or operational validation evidence is reported.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: The paper reports generic V&V support, testing requirements, lifecycle I&T coverage, and prior simulations/trade studies, but no EPS verification artifacts integrated into the model. direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi.quote: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is the formalized application of modeling to support system requirements, design, analysis, verification and validation activities beginning in the conceptual design phase and continuing throughout development and later life cycle phases.
At the core of MBSE is the development of the system model that helps integrate other discipline-specific engineering models and simulations.
The project's application of MBSE uses the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) and graphical modeling tools from No Magic.
These logical elements can be reused for specifying a mission specific CubeSat.
The reference model can support all life cycle stages for a CubeSat mission.
The model also supports all phases of operations: pre-launch integration and test, launch, early orbit checkout, and full mission operations.

Two trade studies were demonstrated: 1) On-board energy level as a function of solar panel area and maximum battery capacity and 2) quantity of data downlinked as a function of orbital altitude and ground station network.
In addition to the model file, the distribution will include video recordings that explain and walk through the model and its components.
The future plans include: (i) refining the CubeSat Reference Model to include additional details for each of the model elements, (ii) verifying the correctness of the model

MBSE holds the promise of reducing the burden of systems engineering tasks, which is beneficial to small CubeSat teams, and a properly designed reference model can serve as a checklist to these teams and promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.

evidence.quote: Requirements Modeling Language (RML) is a collection of diagrams used to model software from the business analysis or product management perspective [12]. RML is concerned with a project's goals and objectives, instead of complex system design models (which is the focus of UML and SySML) [13].

RMM contains multiple levels of mapping that map process flow steps to requirements, requirements to business rules, business objectives to features, features to requirements, requirements to code, and requirements to test cases, as illustrated in Fig. 1.

evidence.quote: Developing cyber-physical systems such as CubeSats requires dynamic engagements of stakeholders, developers, tester, analysts, and project managers. With their different backgrounds, the technicality of analyzing functional and nonfunctional requirements may lead to miscommunication between groups. Thus, applying requirements modeling language (RML) into an engineering system development project will enhance the quality of requirements as well as ease the analysis and elicitation processes.
A Requirements Mapping Matrix (RMM) is best used by a requirement management model tool which can automate the process of checking for missing links [12].

It works as a high-level documentation, which maps and traces user requirements with the corresponding test cases. This is intended to ensure that for each and every requirement there is an adequate level of testing successfully fulfilled.

RMM is intended to reduce the testing time for software applications, ensure the scope of the project is well determined, that its implementation is achieved as per the customer requirements and needs, and that the cost of the project is controlled.

direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi.quote: In this paper, the importance of implementing RML into a project lifecycle of an engineering system (such as a CubeSat system) is described. A case study of using requirements mapping matrix (RMM) for requirements validation and verification of a typical CubeSat system is provided.

Developing cyber-physical systems such as CubeSats requires dynamic engagements of stakeholders, developers, tester, analysts, and project managers. With their different backgrounds, the technicality of analyzing functional and nonfunctional requirements may lead to miscommunication between groups. Thus, applying requirements modeling language (RML) into an engineering system development project will enhance the quality of requirements as well as ease the analysis and elicitation processes.

RMM contains multiple levels of mapping that map process flow steps to requirements, requirements to business rules, business objectives to features, features to requirements, requirements to code, and requirements to test cases, as illustrated in Fig. 1.

It works as a high-level documentation, which maps and traces user requirements with the corresponding test cases. This is intended to ensure that for each and every requirement there is an adequate level of testing successfully fulfilled.
The corresponding RMM matrix with the code and tests mapped to requirements for the NDSAT (example satellite concept) CubeSat Radio and Camera systems is depicted in Fig. 5.
Test Case Description: Test the OBC's ability to save images taken by the camera; Test Scenario: Have the OBC retrieve an image from the camera and save it to disk; Test Case Result: Pass.

RQ1.rationale: The paper provides a general small-satellite/space-system modeling framework with EPS example, but it is not narrowly about nanosatellite/EPS reference modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: The paper claims traceability, reusability/reproducibility, consistency, early validation, integration-cost reduction, and technical robustness, including EPS power simulations, but outcome evidence is mostly single-case and not EPS-outcome-specific.

RQ3.rationale: The framework integrates pre-physical simulation-based verification and requirements linkage, including EPS power verification, but it does not model detailed EPS verification procedures, test cases, or verification matrices.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper cites prior CubeSat/small-satellite MBSE/reference-model work (e.g., Kaslow/Spangelo, ColStar, open-source CubeSat design) but presents MOSAiC/FIRE-EYE as its own open-source Capella/ARCADIA plus simulation framework. No duplicate reference-model lineage is apparent from the paper.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Address fragmentation between descriptive MBSE architecture models and dynamic/domain-specific simulations by creating MOSAiC, an open-source, model-and-simulation framework that maintains traceability, consistency, and early validation across architecture, operations, and simulation artifacts.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Four hierarchical ARCADIA-aligned levels: Actors, System, Subsystem, Components. The case begins with stakeholders/operational needs, then black-box system functions and ConOps, logical subsystem architecture, and physical component architecture. Simulations start from low-fidelity overall parameters and progressively add mode transitions, subsystem modes, reconfigurations, component constraints, and detailed EPS/TTC data.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The method can begin with coarse parameters (mass, volume, power consumption, timing, mass envelopes) and incrementally refines behavior through ConOps states, operating modes, mode transition conditions, and component properties. It still requires mission scenario assumptions, PVMT property values, orbital/visibility inputs, and subsystem/component parameters for executable analyses.

key_evidence_quotes.quote: This module—and more broadly the framework—is structured around four hierarchical modeling levels, in line with the ARCADIA method: (i) Actors; (ii) System; (iii) Subsystem; (iv) Components.
key_evidence_quotes.location: Section 3.1 System and Operation Modeling Module

key_evidence_quotes.quote: Simulation models are developed incrementally, starting with low-fidelity representations based on coarse overall parameters, such as general subsystem mass, volume, and power consumption.
At the most granular level, the Component level introduces physical constraints, physical behavior, and performance requirements.
key_evidence_quotes.location: Section 3.1 System and Operation Modeling Module

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: MOSAiC is presented as a reusable framework/workflow rather than only the FIRE-EYE mission model. The paper explicitly claims applicability beyond a specific space application, uses layered abstraction from stakeholder needs to components, emphasizes interfaces/data exchanges between MBSE and simulations, and makes models/code publicly available. Do not code low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model because dynamic, time-dependent simulations are central; do not code specific-mission model with reusable method only because the framework itself is claimed adaptable beyond the case.

evidence.quote: This paper presents the first version of the unified Modeling and Simulation (M&S) framework MOSAiC ... which connects MBSE with open source, multi-domain simulation environments, with the goal of improving traceability, reusability, and fidelity in the system lifecycle.
Even though this framework is not restricted to a specific space application, it can be especially effective in the field of small-satellite missions
It covers several abstraction layers, from stakeholder-level needs to component-level design
interfacing with simulation tools through standardized data exchanges and co-simulation strategies
All models and codes presented in this work are available in a public repository

evidence_quotes.quote: As presented in the following sections, it is composed of two modules: the (i) System and Operation Modeling module and (ii) Analysis and Simulation module.
The initial Operational Analysis (OA) involved identifying and structuring the mission's stakeholders

At the Logical Architecture (LA) level and, with an increased level of detail, at the Physical Architecture (PA) level, dynamic and domain-specific simulations were integrated into the system model using the proposed framework.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_data_flow: Capella/ARCADIA is the authoritative MBSE model. PVMT enriches Capella elements with mass, power, volume, margins, orbit, mode and component properties. A custom Python parser extracts parameters, exchanges, modes, transitions, and realization links from Capella to feed domain simulations for orbit/access, power, link/data budgets, and mixed LA/PA resolution analyses. Simulation results and requirements verification feed back into architecture decisions.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_lifecycle_continuity: Continuity is maintained through ARCADIA levels, explicit cross-referencing of architecture with mission phases and modes, PVMT properties, and Capella realization links between LA and PA. Semantic continuity is demonstrated conceptually and through the parser but not verified by a formal standard conformance test.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Supports virtual system/subsystem interaction and pre-hardware feasibility checks; concrete software/hardware integration, HIL, flat-sat, environmental test, or flight readiness are not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: All models and code are reported as available in a public repository under GNU GPLv3 at https://gitlab1.polito.it/aer-se-public/MOSAiC. The framework is described as fully open source and based on Capella plus an open simulation pipeline.

evidence_quotes.quote: The Analysis and Simulation module uses the multi-level architectural and operational Modeling module as the central source of truth

The custom parser was specifically implemented to interface directly with the extended logical architecture towards the automated extraction of user-defined attributes embedded through the PVMT extension.
the parser was designed to interpret both architectural and behavioral elements at varying levels of maturity. It did so by leveraging the realization links defined in Capella

eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_representation_and_link: EPS-related requirements are not listed in a requirements table, but the paper describes power generation/storage/regulation/distribution functions and links component properties, operational modes, battery capacity, duty cycles, and power budgets to simulations that verify quantitative constraints before implementation.
eps_verification_specific.evidence_verification_integrated_in_mode: Verification is integrated into the model-to-simulation workflow: PVMT properties are attached to Capella elements, the parser extracts model data and OMs, and simulations verify preconditions, power balance, battery capacity, and communication feasibility. The paper does not show a separate verification matrix or test procedure model.

evidence_quotes.quote: These functions are then translated into concrete architectural elements, shown in Figure 13, where solar panels, batteries, and power distribution units are physically instantiated and interconnected.
By simulating mission execution over time and tracking the activation of modes, it was possible to verify whether preconditions for each OM were satisfied

evidence.quote: Unlike earlier qualitative/exploratory phases, this stage features a direct linkage between formal requirement specifications and simulation results.

synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq1: MOSAiC offers a general ARCADIA/Capella framework for small-satellite/space mission modeling across stakeholder, system, subsystem, and component levels. It handles limited early knowledge by starting with low-fidelity mass/volume/power/timing parameters and refining toward component-level operational modes and simulations.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq2: Claimed outcomes include traceability, reusability/reproducibility, consistency, interoperability, early validation, decision support, risk reduction, reliability/agility of the design process, and reduced integration costs. Evidence is strongest for executable power/data simulation outputs and open repository availability; weak for cost/schedule/defect/effort claims.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq3: The framework integrates pre-physical simulation-based verification into the system/EPS model through PVMT properties, Capella modes, parser extraction, requirements linkage, and dynamic power/link/orbit simulations. However, it does not provide verification matrices, formal test procedures, HIL/SIL, flat-sat, environmental, or flight evidence.
limitations_gaps_stated_by_authors: Future work will expand simulation capability with refined orbital/environmental modeling, automated requirement tracing, automated CAD generation, time-aware thermal analyses, and HIL/digital twin approaches.

The method is useful for system-level conceptual data organization but not a reusable open reference model.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_and_data_flow: IDM-CIC defines the satellite/system/subsystem description and basic geometry and stores power-budget data. Simu-CIC defines the mission scenario and generates ephemeris. IDM-Power allocates IDM-CIC power-budget consumptions to modes and outputs a temporal power profile. Flows Manager converts Simu-CIC CCSDS-like ephemeris data into energy flows. Opalis combines the EPS architecture model, power profile and energy flows to run energy-balance simulations. IDM-View/IDM-Plot can visualize aspects of the system.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity: Continuity is claimed through a common database and standard/CCSDS-like file formats. Semantic continuity is demonstrated for power-budget-to-mode-to-profile and ephemeris-to-energy-flow transformations, but exact schemas and model semantics are not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Supports preliminary electrical architecture choices and component sizing; no direct hardware/software integration, flat-sat, manufacturing, or test readiness is demonstrated.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: Tools and data flow are named, but model files, scenario files, scripts, precise schemas, and public repositories are not reported. Opalis is described as proprietary but open and CNES-developed.
